title: Finite image filtration and convergence transported to an invertible cocone
statement:
Let $X$ be a type-zero exact couple in an abelian category [def-sp-exact-couple], with $D^{p,q}=0$ for $q<a$ and $E^{p,q}=0$ for $p<0$ or $q<a$. Let $L$ be any limiting cycles and boundaries [def-sp-convergence]. Suppose a cocone $j_{n,q}:D^{n-q,q}\to H^n$ has invertible component $c_n$ at $q=n$, and its nonnegative-index maps are incoming alpha iterates followed by $c_n$. There are decreasing filtrations [def-sp-filtration] $F_A$ on $D^{0,n}$ and $F_H$ on $H^n$, with $F_A^p$ the incoming-alpha image for $p\ge0$, $F_A^p=\top$ for $p\le0$, and $F_H=F_A.image(c_n)$ [def-sp-image-filtration]. The steps $F_H^p$ are the images of $j_{n,n-p}$, are top for $p\le0$, and bottom for $p\ge n-a+1$. These filtrations are finite, exhaustive, separated and complete for the inverse-limit quotient tower. For $p<0$ their graded pieces and the infinite page vanish. The cocone is a diagonal colimit with object $H^n$, and $X$ converges to it with limiting subobjects $L$.

Exact Lean interface:
```lean
theorem abutment_image_filtration {B : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂} B] [Abelian B] (X : BigradedExactCouple B 0) (a : ℤ) (hDzero : ∀ p q : ℤ, q < a → IsZero (X.D p q)) (hEzero : ∀ p q : ℤ, (p < 0 ∨ q < a) → IsZero (X.E p q)) (L : X.LimitSubobjects) (H : ℤ → B) (j : ∀ n q : ℤ, X.D (n - q) q ⟶ H n) (c : ∀ n : ℤ, X.D 0 n ⟶ H n) (hc : ∀ n : ℤ, c n = eqToHom (by congr 1; omega) ≫ j n n) (hiso : ∀ n : ℤ, IsIso (c n)) (hcomm : ∀ n p : ℤ, X.alphaDiagonal n p ≫ eqToHom (by congr 1; omega) ≫ j n (n - p) = eqToHom (by congr 1; omega) ≫ j n (n - (p + 1))) (hnorm : ∀ (n p : ℤ) (hp : 0 ≤ p), eqToHom (by congr 1 <;> omega) ≫ j n (n - p) = X.incomingAlphaIter p.toNat 0 n ≫ c n) : ∃ (FA : ∀ n : ℤ, DecreasingFiltration (X.D 0 n)) (FH : ∀ n : ℤ, DecreasingFiltration (H n)), (∀ n p : ℤ, 0 ≤ p → (FA n).step p = imageSubobject (X.incomingAlphaIter p.toNat 0 n)) ∧ (∀ n p : ℤ, p ≤ 0 → (FA n).step p = ⊤) ∧ (∀ n : ℤ, FH n = (FA n).image (c n)) ∧ (∀ n p : ℤ, (FH n).step p = imageSubobject (j n (n - p))) ∧ (∀ n p : ℤ, p ≤ 0 → (FH n).step p = ⊤) ∧ (∀ n p : ℤ, n - a + 1 ≤ p → (FH n).step p = ⊥) ∧ (∀ n : ℤ, (FH n).IsFinite ∧ (FH n).IsExhaustive ∧ (FH n).IsSeparated ∧ BigradedExactCouple.IsInverseLimit (FH n)) ∧ (∀ p q : ℤ, p < 0 → IsZero ((FH (p + q)).gradedPiece p) ∧ IsZero (X.pageInfinity L p q)) ∧ ∃ (AH : ∀ n : ℤ, X.AlphaColimit n) (hAH : ∀ n : ℤ, (AH n).obj = H n), (∀ n p : ℤ, (AH n).ι p ≫ eqToHom (hAH n) = eqToHom (by congr 1; omega) ≫ j n (n - p)) ∧ X.ConvergesTo L AH
```

proof.text:
Take the normalized diagonal colimits A supplied by negative-E vanishing.
Factor the prescribed cocone through A using its universal property. Its component
at zero and the normalization identify the factor with eqToHom(hA) followed by c,
so this factor is invertible. Transport A along this isomorphism to obtain AH,
and along eqToHom(hA) to obtain AA with object D(0,n). Define FA and FH to be
the image filtrations of AA and AH. The positive normalization gives the
incoming-alpha image formula for FA; image pushforward gives FH=FA.image(c).
The transported cocone gives the j-image formula. Negative-index cocone maps
are invertible, giving top for p<=0; when p>=n-a+1 the source D(p,n-p) is zero,
giving bottom. These bounds prove finiteness, exhaustiveness and separatedness.
Beyond the bottom bound the cokernel projections are invertible; factor a
compatible quotient cone through one such projection and use integer induction
to prove all its equations. Cancellation there proves uniqueness.
Construct the isomorphism between the transported and original graded pieces
by cokernel.mapIso on the two imageSubobjectCompIso maps. Cancellation of the
image arrows proves the square commutes and that the canonical graded maps
commute with this isomorphism. Half-plane weak convergence for A then gives
weak convergence for AH by invariance of kernels under postcomposition by an
isomorphism. Sharp bounds give regularity, and the preceding filtration and
inverse-limit properties complete convergence. For p<0 both adjacent steps
are top, making their inclusion invertible and its cokernel zero. The canonical
weak-convergence comparison transports this zero-object assertion to E_infinity.
